plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap (greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-ins, and a defined Excluded Claims list in 21.3 covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement. Check adequacy of cap size and that fee obligations are unlimited (21.3 last sentence). Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

No indemnification section appears in the outline (numbering jumps from 19 to 21; Section 20 and its referenced 20.5 are absent). Cross-references in sec-9.3 (to Section 20.5) and Excluded Claims in sec-21.3 assume an indemnity exists — treat as missing unless an unlisted Section 20 surfaces in the body text.

sec-12.4-2 imposes a broad 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer — direct conflict with the rule and with sec-12.3, which disclaims any non-compete. Flag sec-12.4-2; cite sec-12.3 as the internally inconsistent, correct position.

sec-12.3 preserves supplier freedom, but sec-7.2 (first 7.2) requires Customer to disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider — a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal. Assess under this rule; the pricing-disclosure aspect belongs to MFN, so avoid double-flagging the same term.

The first sec-7.2 obliges Customer to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers — an MFN running against us, contrary to sec-12.3's disclaimer. Wrong direction; flag the disclosure/matching obligation here if the exclusivity framing is handled under EXCLUSIVITY.

sec-12.4 bars Customer from soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out, hire ban not just solicit, and one-way. Contrast sec-12.3, which preserves hiring from general recruitment.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency, and specific-trigger termination (9.1–9.3, 9.5); sec-2.1 expressly negates reduction or termination rights. No convenience termination for Customer appears — likely missing. Note sec-8.2 non-renewal and sec-27.3 force-majeure exit as partial, non-substitute exits.

sec-8.2 gives 30-day non-renewal notice with a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if not sent; sec-8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant — confirm before flagging.

sec-28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list — and directly conflicts with sec-28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction. Flag sec-28.1 and reconcile with 28.2; sec-28.3 escalation is acceptable.

sec-24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; sec-24.2 restricts Vendor; sec-24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. Favourable to us — verify and do not flag.

sec-14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP, but sec-14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — fails the 'we own what we pay for' position. Check interaction with sec-13.2/14.3 perpetual licence, which does not cure revocability or ownership.

sec-13.1–13.3 cover Affiliates and contractors, are perpetual for paid-up material, and limit revocation to material uncured breach after cure opportunity. Tension with sec-14.2's revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence — address the revocability there under IP rather than double-flagging.

sec-22.1 limits audits to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor; sec-22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent a >5% underpayment and bars system/data access. Likely compliant.

No liquidated-damages or penalty payable by Customer is evident; sec-7.3 protects disputed amounts and bars interest on amounts not due. The take-or-pay shortfall exposure in sec-2.1 is best handled under MINCOMMIT. Likely no separate LD clause.

sec-19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, full term for hosted Services), malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties; sec-19.4 provides repair/re-perform then termination and refund, expressly non-exclusive for key claims; sec-19.5 disclaimer is limited. Likely compliant.

sec-18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; sec-18.2 covers certificates, primacy, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Present — check limits against the healthcare data profile before commenting.

sec-2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment for three years expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — squarely against the rule and contradicted by sec-12.3's no-minimum-volume disclaimer. Primary flag; interacts with the absent T4C right.

Section 10 addresses access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and refunds, and sec-16.5 covers return/destruction of Confidential Information, but no express transition-assistance period or Customer Data extraction/return-in-usable-format obligation appears (Section 11, cross-referenced in sec-16.5, is not in the outline). Assess whether the data-return and migration-help elements are materially missing.
